tier_reason: The README table (1920x1080x24-bit image, AMD Ryzen 7 3700X) compares libpng 1.6 with pngenc single- and multi-threaded and the numbers match the record, but it is first-party and states no compiler, flags or harness. The repo has pngenc-only timing tests (tests/perf_mt.c, tests/perf_huffman.c, which read an unpublished data.bin image) and no libpng timing code, so it cannot be A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (ms, libpng 1.6 vs pngenc 1 thread vs pngenc multi-threaded, 1920x1080x24-bit image, Ryzen 7 3700X): Uncompressed 9 vs 0.8 vs 0.2; Huffman Only 82 vs 7.3 vs 1.2; RLE 84 vs 30 vs 4; Full LZ77 ~150 vs N/A vs N/A. That is about 11x (uncompressed), 11x (Huffman only) and 2.8x (RLE) single-threaded, and 45x, 68x and 21x multi-threaded (derived from page data). README says 'up to an order of magnitude faster' at 'the same compression rates' as libpng/zlib.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the README table. The repo's CMakeLists.txt builds pngenc with -march=native -mtune=native -O3 -fopenmp (GCC/Clang) or /openmp /arch:AVX2 (MSVC); how libpng was built is not stated.
corrections.caveats: Single first-party table, one unpublished image and one CPU; compiler, flags and the libpng timing harness are not published (tests/perf_mt.c times pngenc only, on a data.bin file that is not in the repo). PNG trade-off: pngenc only implements stored, Huffman-only (Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY) and RLE deflate with a fixed horizontal (Sub) row filter (no filter for the uncompressed mode), so its output is much larger than libpng at its default LZ77 level; the README's Full LZ77 row (libpng ~150 ms) has no pngenc counterpart, and the table gives no file sizes to back the 'same compression rates' claim. The comparison is against libpng's low-effort strategies, which the README itself calls a valid trade-off. The multi-threaded column uses OpenMP across the image, while libpng is single-threaded. A later mode (PNGENC_AUTO, Huffman-only falling back to RLE) is not in the README table. Hobby project for learning, per the README.

notes: Numbers, hardware, license (zlib license; crc32 code by Mark Adler under a zlib-compatible license), 3 stars and last commit 2024-08-10 (stale) all check out. The speed comes from skipping LZ77 entirely, so it suits fast snapshot or screenshot dumps rather than size-competitive PNGs.

tier_reason: The README and PERFORMANCE.md numbers match the record and come from public benchmark code (tools/bench_compare.c, tools/bench_encode.c, .github/workflows/nightly.yml) run on GitHub-hosted runners whose CPU models are logged in gh-pages bench/data.js. Compiler versions are never stated (only gcc/clang/MSVC cl on the runner images) and the optimisation flags are only CMake's implicit Release defaults, so it stays first-party C, just short of A.

corrections.license: None stated: no LICENSE file (raw LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt and COPYING all return 404), the GitHub page shows no license, and README.md, include/ptpng.h and CMakeLists.txt give no terms
corrections.baseline: Decoder: libpng 1.6 (vendored libpng16 branch) with zlib-ng 2.2.4 in ZLIB_COMPAT mode. Encoder: libpng with the vendored stock zlib (develop branch) at level 6 and libpng with zlib-ng 2.2.4 at level 6, both with PNG_ALL_FILTERS adaptive filtering.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README: decoder geometric-mean speedup over libpng + zlib-ng 2.2.4 across 27 cases is 1.80x Linux x64 (27/27 faster), 1.64x Windows x64 (26/27), 1.59x Linux ARM64 (27/27), 1.62x macOS ARM64 (27/27) and 1.46x Windows ARM64 (26/27) in the 30 Sep 2026 nightly run 36753946386. Encoder (1 Oct change, nightly run 36791257328 per PERFORMANCE.md) averages 2.25-2.98x stock zlib level 6 and 1.14-1.52x zlib-ng level 6 across five platforms, faster than zlib-ng in only 4-6 of the 9 fixtures per platform, with PNGs at most 2.4% larger than zlib-ng level 6.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build with no explicit -O level in CMakeLists.txt (CMake's defaults, -O3 -DNDEBUG for gcc/clang and /O2 for MSVC), plus per-file -mavx2 or /arch:AVX2 and -mpclmul -msse2 kernels. The nightly matrix uses gcc (ubuntu24 x64 and arm64 images), clang (macos-14) and MSVC cl (win25-vs2026, win11-vs2026-arm64); compiler versions are not stated. PERFORMANCE.md quotes -O3 for paired runs and MSVC /O2 /Ob2 for local runs.
corrections.hardware: GitHub-hosted runners logged in gh-pages bench/data.js. 30 Sep decoder run 36753946386: Linux x64 and Windows x64 AMD EPYC 7763 (4 logical CPUs), Linux ARM64 Neoverse-N2, Windows ARM64 Cobalt 100, macOS Apple M1 (Virtual). Encoder run 36791257328: same, except Windows x64 was AMD EPYC 9V45. Local runs used an Intel Core i7-1355U.
corrections.workload: PNG decode (27 cases: nine fixtures in native, RGB8 and RGBA8 output, median of 12 alternating rounds) and PNG encode (nine generated fixtures, median of five rotated rounds with a round-trip check) on five GitHub-hosted CI platforms. Fixtures are generated gradients, graphics and random noise at 3200x2400, except the two RGBA16 fixtures and noise_rgba8, which are 1024x768.
corrections.caveats: No license file or license terms, so the code is reference only. Very new repository (0 stars; commits from 2026-09-24 to 2026-09-30); numbers change nightly and the README says to compare ratios only within a run because hosted runner CPUs change. Fixtures are synthetic (gradients, graphics, noise) and the project says they do not establish a fastest-in-the-world claim. Decoder loses on noise-to-RGB8 on both Windows platforms. PNG encoder trade-offs: it only writes non-interlaced gray, gray+alpha, RGB and RGBA at 8 or 16 bits (no palette, packed-sample or metadata output, so palette images expand to RGBA8); its files are up to 2.4% larger than zlib-ng level 6; and zlib-ng level 6 is faster on 3-5 of the 9 fixtures per platform (for example 0.76x on photo_rgb8 in the local i7-1355U table). Library calls must be serialized across threads because internal tables and dispatch state are shared. Compiler versions are not stated.

notes: No LICENSE confirmed on github.com and in raw paths; usability stays reference. The benchmarks look fair: the reference encoders use PNG_ALL_FILTERS at the same level, every encode round-trips and is compared by memcmp, and CI checks byte parity with libpng; no correctness bug was found behind the published numbers. A compiler-version statement would make this tier A.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C. The README table runs public benchmark code (src/qoibench.cpp, which compiles qoi.h and qoixx into one binary and cross-checks decodes with memcmp) on the public QOI benchmark suite. The Makefile states the flags (-std=c++2a -O3 -march=native -mtune=native, unchanged since Feb 2022), and the README gives the g++ version and CPU model for each of the seven machines.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README (grand total for the QOI benchmark suite, 20 iterations): on Intel Core i9-10900 with g++ 11.1.0, qoi decodes in 2.2389 ms (207.326 mpps) and encodes in 2.5434 ms (182.504 mpps), against qoixx at 1.3477 ms (344.431 mpps) and 1.5255 ms (304.280 mpps), about 1.66x decode and 1.67x encode. Across all seven machines qoixx is 1.37-1.66x faster at decoding and 1.47-1.76x faster at encoding (derived from page data), with identical output size (463 KB, 28.2%).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: g++ per machine as listed in the README: 11.1.0 (i9-10900, Kryo 585), 11.0.0 20200622 experimental (Ryzen 7 2700X), 12.0.0 20211219 experimental (Ryzen 7 3800X), 11.2.0 MSYS2 ucrt64 (Ryzen 9 3950X, Windows), 11.2.0 (Graviton3, Apple M1 Max). Makefile CXXFLAGS: -std=c++2a -O3 -march=native -mtune=native. qoi.h is compiled into the same qoibench binary with the same flags.
corrections.caveats: Baseline is the qoi.h reference implementation, not libpng/libwebp, so this qualifies only through the QOI entry (phoboslab/qoi vs libpng). The README numbers date from 2022 (benchmark sections added March-June 2022) against the qoi.h revision of that time; the README gives no commit for them. Per the README, the decoder is a scalar implementation and 'with some input, original implementation is faster', and MSVC-built decoders are slow (FAQ recommends MinGW-w64). Results use -march=native builds and need C++20.

notes: Not a duplicate of the phoboslab/qoi record: qoixx is an independent C++20 re-implementation of the QOI format (its own 1400-line qoixx.hpp with AVX2/NEON/SVE encoders), not a wrapper or port of qoi.h. Only the benchmark harness is adapted from qoi's qoibench, hence LICENSES/qoi.LICENSE. baseline_in_list stays false. MIT, 42 stars, last commit 2026-09-29 (active).
